expectations.text: Rejects the single big-cutover release in favour of a staged sequence.
expectations.evidence: "Verdict: don't do one big cutover" and a phased table (Phase 0 to 4 plus buffer) with shadow, warn, brownout and enforce per cohort.

expectations.text: Gives the build order: protocol core first, then scope taxonomy and consent screen, then registration and verification, then advanced hardening.
expectations.evidence: The phases are organised by deprecation and rollout timing. Scopes are deferred as a 'dated roadmap item' and the verification program is 'Start with publisher identity verification'. The protocol, then scope and consent, then registration and verification, then hardening order is never given.

expectations.text: Recommends modelling compliance as separately named, independently toggleable boolean gates per requirement (PKCE enforcement, exact redirect matching, rotation, and so on) rather than a single 'OAuth 2.1 mode' flag.
expectations.evidence: "Use one named, independently toggleable gate per requirement. This is the Django OAuth Toolkit COMPLIANT_BCP_RFC9700_* pattern."

expectations.text: Justifies the per-requirement gates by auditability: a partial rollout can point at exactly which requirements are and are not enforced yet.
expectations.evidence: "The gate history doubles as audit evidence." The control matrix has 'One row per requirement, with the gate flag, the automated test, and the evidence location.'

expectations.text: Requires removing the implicit grant and the resource-owner password grant, migrating the dashboard and the iOS app to authorization_code with PKCE.
expectations.evidence: "Migrate your own dashboard from implicit to code + PKCE"; "Remove implicit for third parties"; "Hard-disable password grant"; iOS uses "ASWebAuthenticationSession" (system browser).

expectations.text: Replaces prefix redirect matching with exact string matching.
expectations.evidence: "Enforce exact redirect matching and PKCE by cohort" and "Redirects: Run exact matching in shadow first."

expectations.text: States that a non-rotating, never-expiring refresh token held by a public client is banned under OAuth 2.1, not merely a weaker option.
expectations.evidence: Only "Confidential clients: Never-expiring tokens will fail review." It does not say this is banned for public clients under 2.1.

expectations.text: Requires designing the refresh-token family relationship into newly issued grants, noting that retrofitting family grouping onto an already-issued ungrouped population is materially harder.
expectations.evidence: It describes token families and lazy migration ('Legacy tokens become family roots on first use'). It never says to design families into new grants or that retrofitting grouping is harder.

expectations.text: Cites the forced-retrofit precedent: a 2025 OAuth-token campaign against a connected app hit more than 700 organizations and led a major platform to mandate PKCE and refresh-token rotation on all connected apps, with de-listing as the penalty.
expectations.evidence: No mention of any such campaign or precedent anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: States that what the auditor gets shown is a discovery document plus a conformance pass verified by test, not an assertion of compliance.
expectations.evidence: "Discovery document: grant_types_supported has no implicit or password..." and "Negative conformance tests in CI, plus a prod smoke test"; also "A release is not evidence."
